column8: Fri 20 Nov: 3c or 3e pedigree for why a share figure stays pencil; the journal's own figures (abstract 4.3% against 0.8%, Table I 4.32 against 0.75), read again at source today, replace H4-059's draft 4.73/1.5; price gains only, so never called a total return.

Fri 20 Nov: store; closures were common (11 of 39 markets died for good, checked at source), but they cluster in one war and one depression; the 1931 sentence's end is cut in the copy read, so counts only, no phrase.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3, one clause on one world fund (and the outside evidence behind the copout's after, never told as part of the team's own moment): the world index with dead markets made 4.04% real against the US's 4.32% with volatility 11.05 against 15.83 (Table VI read at source); always with row 6's break, since 1920's world was about half American.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3 with row 3, one figure pair at most: in dollars the world with its losers made 7.25% against the US's 6.95% (Table VII read at source); flattered by other currencies rising, so never alone; the 25 basis points is the non-US index's bias, the global's is 7; COSPONSOR tag is wrong.
Fri 20 Nov: 2.3 mechanism, quote checked at source (markets that die tend to have less weight when they do so); pairs with row 11 as the live case; holds only for a slow decline (row 15).

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3, the honest break a finance judge will raise: the 1921 world fund did well partly by holding the survivor, and VT is 62.4% US; source-level twin of Q175-010's point, so one of the two, said as VT holding the market's current guess.
Fri 20 Nov: the authors' own sentence for row 3's lower swings (risk reduction rather than increased returns, read at source); travels with row 3 as its quote, never a separate point.

Fri 20 Nov: store, 2.3 at most: in 1899 the UK was 24.2% of world shares and the US 14.5%, the US 60.5% in 2024, so a world fund's weights followed the survivor with no one choosing; one of this or Q6d-009 (Japan in 1987), never both.
Fri 20 Nov: DMS's success bias is H7-042's point (the US premium may not generalise); also fifteen houses is now seventeen (card Q146).

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3 or store: Russia deleted from FTSE indexes at the open on 7 Mar 2022, Moscow-listed names at zero (notice read again at source); fix four years to nearly five (Mar 2022 to Jan 2027), and GDRs went at close price unless suspended or sanctioned, so never every Russian company at zero (the card's idea 2 says so).

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3 with row 5: Russia had shrunk from 6.2% (2012) to 1.4% of FTSE's emerging index before the write-off, the mechanism live; its causes (2014 sanctions, falling prices) say a sudden death gives no such warning.

Fri 20 Nov: store; the watch list was a review of market access for promotion, not a call on survival, so it breaks under its own column: say only that six months before the write-off Russia was on the watch list for promotion, never that the index keeper could not pick the survivor; 3f names no outside source (panel 4) and the team did not know it on 5 Oct, so never inside the copout moment (standing order 22).

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3 one clause, a country's death cost a world fund about a fifth of one percent (0.19% All-World, 0.18% ACWI); VT's own Russian weight unfound, so never print $56 to $104 as VT's loss; Keel arithmetic on the plan's $29,594 checks.
Fri 20 Nov: store; VT's manager dropped Russia within a week with no action by holders; a statement, not an audited VT figure.

Fri 20 Nov: 3c or 3e, why no stated figure rests on VT until the move: a big market's sudden break (Japan 95% real 1944-49, Germany 72%) has no shrinking-weight cushion; both spanned a lost war, so never a forecast for any market.
Fri 20 Nov: References and pedigree only; Brown, Goetzmann and Ross's opening line, quoted at source.

Fri 20 Nov: 3c store, why a historical premium is pencil: with a zero true premium an observed 8 points fits a 50% chance of surviving the century, a true 4 points fits 80% (read at source today); carry Li and Xu's objection (row 23) beside it.

Fri 20 Nov: 3b and 3c, one clause: a market studied because it survived looks as if it always recovers (artifact of survival, (4-pi)/2 limit, read at source today), so IPS l.17's last sentence and the dated move refuse the one pattern survival manufactures, while the half kept may wait to 2033; answers H2-050's weakness; evaluates, adds no rule (CANON A34); real mean reversion may exist (H6-081); no variance ratio in prose.
Fri 20 Nov: store; a disaster that closes a market erases its own evidence; Rietz not read, quotes via Mehra and BGR.
Fri 20 Nov: References pedigree for TNA l.23's growth premium (6.18 points against a model ceiling of 0.35); verified source behind H3-058 and H4-152; never named without the plan's answer (row 26).
Fri 20 Nov: H7-034 already holds the premium's wide standard error and no promise resting on a forecast; this adds only Mehra and Prescott's 1.76; the 3.4% use is row 28's.

Fri 20 Nov: store; the low historical safe rate never enters the plan, because what the payments need is fixed by prices paid in 2027 and 2028 with the extra Treasuries sized for cash waiting earning nothing; never every dollar known (interest is reinvested at unknown rates, SKELETON 2.1).
Fri 20 Nov: 3c store, the critique that must travel with rows 17 and 18 (survival needs implausibly high failure odds to explain the premium); abstracts only, body unverified.

Fri 20 Nov: 3c or 3e assumption: survivorship bites only the side not yet owned; fix her Treasury return is a price paid to what the payments need is fixed by 2027 and 2028 prices, with the extra Treasuries sized for cash waiting earning nothing (reinvestment rates are unknown); never a caveat on Treasuries; inference Keel's.
Fri 20 Nov: J.P. Morgan's own disclaimer (Q6-001) and the 3-year window (Q6-029) already make this point for 3c; Mehra's line adds a famous name only; one clause at most if References needs it.

Fri 20 Nov: 3c's reason in one sentence, the plan is indifferent to the equity premium puzzle; fix VT's top (the top rests on the late-2032 fund bought twice; VT's growth to the move sets how much the move buys) and the unclear disaster clause (a disaster before the move lowers only the top she can state; after it nothing stated moves); new beside H5-001 and Q123-039 only in its three answers.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e store; register figures check (8v: $21,179 at 7.5%, $17,185 at 3.1%), but at 3.1% the top she can state is also one step lower, $110,000, so add it and say never her promises because nothing is stated before the move; forecast-based, so an illustration, never a plan figure; near H5-001.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e or Table 2 note at most; subtracts a century's real price gap from a three-year nominal total return, so restate from the register: the forecast can fall about 4 points, to 3.417% (8v), before the top she can state steps down, more than the whole 3.57-point survivor gap; forecast-based, never a plan figure; extends H2-088 and H4-089.

Fri 20 Nov: store; the bias is small change over three years ($318 of VT, $169 of the unrounded top; 8p's $0.53 slope checks); $2,142 is the rounding gap above $115,000, not the room under the top (WORDS: the margin plus the rounding down); rests on VT at 7.5%, an illustration only.

Fri 20 Nov: store, the card's own honest break: survivorship matters for a century's compounding and decides little over three years, where a bad draw dominates (Q6-025, Q6-029); the $95,000 to $140,000 is the house 1-in-20 stated top (NUMBERS 4), not Table 2.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e store: the NYSE shut 31 Jul to 12 Dec 1914, so a closure delays the move; cannot smudge it is cannot move for a stated figure, banned (NUMBERS 3, an early fund end); under $300 is the central case only (8r: a fall between dates lowers the top in 11.8% to 15.4% of paths); VT and IBTM both trade on exchange; adds no rule (A34).

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3, answers why a world fund but one country's bonds; fix only the dollar's own issuer pays fixed dollars without currency risk (any dollar bond has none; the reason is that the payments are fixed US dollars and the IPS names Treasuries, guaranteed, Book 19) and drop survivor for the Treasury side; near AHA row 2.

Fri 20 Nov: store only, by its own column; adds closure arithmetic (about $1,000 of $29,594 at Taiwan's 3.5%) to H8-134 and H9-105's reason; never stage a Taiwan closure, never a Taiwan-dollar hedge, and doubled is loose.
